summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22% YoY to Rs 356 crore, EBITDA loss narrowed to Rs 20 crore, and FY26 net loss was Rs 1.4 crore versus Rs 133 crore.
summary.overview: Health X Platform reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 356 crore (up 22% YoY, 4% QoQ) with gross margin up to 7.3% from 5.9% and EBITDA loss narrowed to Rs 20 crore from Rs 29 crore. The Q4 PAT loss of Rs 12.9 crore compared with a Rs 17.6 crore profit a year earlier, which management attributed to lower other income and exceptional items. For FY26, revenue was Rs 1,283 crore (up 18%), EBITDA loss was Rs 65 crore, and PAT loss was Rs 1.4 crore. Management also announced a scheme to demerge a finance division into Microsec Resources, launched the JITO private-label genetic medicine category, and guided to Rs 6,000 crore revenue by FY30.

segments.name: Retailer Shakti (B2B)
segments.commentary: Sells to over 62,000 retail pharmacies and partners with more than 700 pharma companies; management says it is running almost at EBITDA breakeven and is contribution-margin positive and covering corporate costs. Non-medicine share is about 2% of sales, targeted at 10% within a year.

segments.name: SastaSundar (B2C)
segments.commentary: Contribution-margin positive per management, with a 18-day working capital cycle and an inventory-light model. Stated plan to scale consumer healthcare; the JITO category is being rolled out here as well.

segments.name: JITO (private-label genetic medicine)
segments.commentary: Launched in FY26 across B2B and B2C with sales of about Rs 30 lakh per month in its launch period, two-thirds from Retailer Shakti and one-third from SastaSundar. Management expects 30-40%+ margins.

guidance_outlook: Revenue target of Rs 6,000 crore by FY30 (Rs 4,000 crore from Retailer Shakti, Rs 2,000 crore from B2C), with EBITDA around 5% and PAT and cash around 4% of revenue at that scale.
FY27 and FY28 ROE expected to be low due to possible losses; FY29 PAT guided at about 3% of revenue (around Rs 120 crore on about Rs 4,500 crore revenue); long-term ROE target about 40%.

June 2026 quarter Retailer Shakti revenue expected at about Rs 400 crore, described as the best quarter in company history; management declined to give formal FY27 guidance but agreed an analyst annualisation of about Rs 1,700 crore is a reasonable stipulation.
Retailer Shakti EBITDA margin guidance of about 1% reiterated for FY27.
Beauty care and personal care categories to roll out on both platforms by 31 December 2026.
Total capex of Rs 234 crore for Udaipur, Lucknow, Patna, Guwahati and additional West Bengal warehouses: Rs 134 crore via bank loans and about Rs 100 crore from treasury.

Warehouse capacity of about 2.5 lakh sq ft currently; about 1 lakh sq ft to go live by 31 March 2027; total capacity to exceed 8 lakh sq ft after further builds. Shift to a new double-capacity Noida/Baruipur warehouse expected around September 2026.

Demerger: Finance Division to be listed as Microsec Resources (1 share for every 3 held in Health X). Health X keeps operating business, SastaSundar HealthBuddy and about Rs 400 crore treasury; Microsec gets about Rs 140 crore of assets (about Rs 100 crore financial investments and about Rs 40 crore real estate at book value).
capex_capacity: Warehousing currently about 2.5 lakh sq ft; more than double the earlier footprint, per management.
Additional 1 lakh sq ft to go live by 31 March 2027; a further 5.52 lakh sq ft planned across Udaipur, Lucknow, Patna, Guwahati and Baruipur, taking total capacity above 8 lakh sq ft.
Noida capacity being doubled; new double-capacity warehouse expected to shift around September 2026.
Plan for about 10,000 smaller warehouses for rapid fulfilment in nearby towns; not yet quantified in capex.
Total capex of Rs 234 crore planned (Rs 134 crore bank debt, about Rs 100 crore treasury).
Management says Rs 6,000 crore revenue can be serviced after the new capacity is in place, but said the current three warehouses alone would not be enough.
demand_pricing: JITO launched in both B2B and B2C; management reports positive surprises, with sales of about Rs 30 lakh per month in its second month. Too early for meaningful conclusions.
JITO is private-label, with margins expected at 30-40%+; management expects to show results from Q3-Q4 FY27.
Transition of HealthBuddy stores into JITO stores caused disruption to branded-medicine sales in Q4, per management.
Hospital channel: management is pitching a next-day emergency backup supply to hospitals, expects 5-6% of hospital purchases could shift to retailers; no credit offered, cash-and-carry only.
West Bengal market share about 5-7% depending on pocket; Northeast growing more than 50% YoY and North India growing 25-30% YoY.
AI products: RetailAir (B2B automated filling centres) and a B2C counselling tool; management says the market is not yet ready and rollout is deferred about six months.

qa_highlights.question: How has JITO been received and what sales is it generating?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 30 lakh per month in sales, two-thirds from Retailer Shakti and one-third from SastaSundar; management says it is too early to draw conclusions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for hospitals and non-pharma categories?
qa_highlights.answer: Hospitals are being approached with a next-day backup supply offer; no credit is extended. Surgical, devices and nutraceuticals are already listed, and personal and beauty care comes by 31 December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How much capital will go into the AI consulting product?
qa_highlights.answer: Total investment of about Rs 150 crore across the stake including B2C, of which about Rs 75 crore is already deployed and about Rs 75 crore more to come.

qa_highlights.question: Why was fulfilment staff moved onto payroll and what is the cost effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Staff were earlier outsourced; they are now on payroll for loyalty and retention, with attrition sharply lower. Management says the net cost impact is roughly nil, since outsourcing fees of 3-4% are offset by internal administration cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale for the Microsec demerger and treasury allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury of about Rs 500 crore in total: Rs 400 crore stays with the operating company for growth capex and working capital; about Rs 100 crore goes to Microsec. Management cited tax efficiency, since treasury income is taxed in Microsec but not in the operating company.

qa_highlights.question: What treasury yield is targeted and how is loss risk managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Stated policy of 10-12% yield per annum versus 7-8% for government bonds; management says there is no capital loss and points to structured deals and NSE dividends.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin and ROE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: At Rs 6,000 crore revenue, EBITDA is targeted at about 5% and PAT and cash at about 4%. FY29 PAT at about 3% of revenue; long-term ROE target about 40%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1% Retailer Shakti EBITDA guidance intact and what is the FY27 revenue run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the 1% guidance; April-May revenue is supporting a June quarter of about Rs 400 crore, but no formal FY27 number was given.

risks_watch: Treasury risk: about Rs 500 crore of treasury, with unquoted shares and AIF/private-credit exposure; management says returns of 10-12% are targeted, but the policy is not detailed.
Execution risk on Rs 234 crore capex and warehouse timelines (1 lakh sq ft by March 2027).
FY27 and FY28 expected to show losses, per management, which may affect the earlier breakeven timeline.
Contribution-margin and tech-cost split not yet disclosed; management promised to start disclosure from the next quarter.
Q4 PAT swung to a loss from profit a year ago; other income and exceptional items are key to reported profit.
Demerger and Microsec's post-listing plans are unresolved; management said any AIF/NBFC revival would wait until after March 2027.
Revenue quarterly variance, with management saying the business is not linear; Q4 SastaSundar growth was muted.

summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, capital efficiency and the Rs 6,000 crore FY30 vision, with management repeatedly calling the company a startup. Notably cautious on near-term items: declined formal FY27 guidance, withheld contribution-margin figures until next quarter, and deferred the AI consulting rollout by about six months. Defensive on treasury risk, where unquoted shares and AIF/private-credit exposure were answered with assurances of "no capital loss" rather than a detailed policy.

growth.why: Management targets Rs 6,000 crore revenue by FY30 and guides June-2026 quarter Retailer Shakti revenue to about Rs 400 crore (analyst annualisation about Rs 1,700 crore, not formal FY27 guidance), backed by Rs 234 crore warehouse capex with about 1 lakh sq ft live by March 2027 and a 5.52 lakh sq ft pipeline, though FY30 path depends on capacity not yet built.
